> ### Recording and recovering operational configuration changes
>
> Applying recommended configuration through a role (yoyodyne-ifd.434.8) preserves the distinction between template history, an authorized change, publication, and observed adoption.
>
> The existing `config.lock` remains a record of what the template originally supplied. Applying an operational setting does not regenerate it, advance it to the current template, or copy the project’s current values into it. A missing baseline remains unknown unless its original contents can be recovered from evidence. Recording a new operational decision does not require inventing that missing history.
>
> Each authorized change has a durable operation identifier and records the deciding role, reason, repository, target file, expected source contents, permitted fields, their prior presence and values, and their requested replacements. Absence, explicit empty values, and inherited values remain distinct. The effective configuration revision supplements this record; it cannot replace source comparison because different source files can produce identical effective settings.
>
> The trusted writer changes only the authorized fields in an isolated candidate. It uses the existing decoder and resolver to validate the complete result. It preserves list order and whole-list replacement semantics. Where a containing mapping replaces an inherited mapping, the candidate must explicitly preserve every unaffected effective member; silently dropping another task is refused. Both the source differences and effective differences must remain within the recorded authorization. Unsupported YAML structures are refused rather than rewritten ambiguously.
>
> The candidate passes protected-path authorization, independent review, and the applicable verification before publication. A configuration change cannot weaken the checks or authority used to approve itself: that change is evaluated under the previously authorized policy and any additional verification its governing design requires.
>
> Retries reconcile the same operation’s candidate, publication, and adoption records before acting. An uncertain publication is investigated before another change is created. Source changes outside the operation require a fresh comparison and review; recovery never overwrites them with an earlier whole-file copy.
>
> Drift retains its existing template comparison and separately shows the operational decision that explains a project value. A conflict is assigned to the owner of that setting through the ownership resolver; “conflicting” does not itself mean the operator must decide. Doctor reports published-but-unadopted settings separately from invalid configuration and unknown adoption.
>
> Adoption is established by the relevant running reader reporting the effective configuration revision and its process identity after successful loading. Writing the file, publishing a commit, or recomputing a digest is insufficient. Restoring prior settings is another recorded, reviewed change against current contents, preserving intervening unrelated edits.

>

A role decides permitted operational values; the harness records the decision, delivers a reviewed change, and reports whether the intended readers have adopted it.

> **Permitted fields and their owners.** Trusted Go code holds a closed registry of permitted configuration fields. Each entry identifies the exact field, its type, validation, deciding role, permitted effects and adoption boundary. A field’s presence in the configuration schema does not make it writable through this capability.

> | --- | --- |
> | Checks, landing checks and path checks | Development manager, preserving required verification. Narrowing coverage must follow the applicable architect design. |
> | Developer model mappings and operational model, model-version and effort fields on existing developer or management agents and tasks | Development manager, within standing provider eligibility, spending directions and supported adapter behavior. > | Preferences within existing developer slots | Lead Product Manager, preserving slot count, identity and eligible endpoints. |
> | Interval, enablement and turn limit of an existing recurring task | Lead Product Manager, preserving mandatory coverage and the task’s identity, agent, prompt, workflow and remit. |
> | Check time limits and operational polling, drain and stall limits | Development manager, preserving enclosing budgets and required verification. |
> | Repair-attempt, integration-retry and transient-relaunch limits | Lead Product Manager; changing a limit never erases spent attempts or independently authorizes another attempt. |
> | Usage-pause, overload and brake thresholds, cooldowns and escalation intervals | Lead Product Manager; changing a value never releases an existing hold or supplies a triage decision. |
>

Reviewer configuration and repair-cap grants are excluded.

It accepts a project, an existing configuration target, expected source revision, typed field changes and a reason. The harness derives the caller from the conversation and checks the deciding authority for every field. A request spanning several owners needs recorded authorization from each owner for the same proposed values; otherwise the whole request is refused.

>

Its protected-path grant names the exact file and permitted fields; it never grants the whole `.yoyodyne` directory and cannot include `.yoyodyne/roles/`. The trusted writer preserves unrelated source content and effective values. It uses the existing decoder and resolution rules, preserving list order and the distinction between absent, explicitly empty and inherited values. Unsupported source structures are refused rather than rewritten approximately.

A source change since authorization requires a fresh comparison and renewed authorization for any changed effect; an effective-configuration digest alone does not authorize overwriting a changed source.

>
> **Compatibility and adoption.** Validation establishes that the intended installed readers support the proposed fields and values. Schema acceptance alone does not prove provider model availability or actual effort support. If compatibility cannot be established, adoption remains pending with the missing evidence named.

> Publication and adoption are separate facts. The harness records the committed configuration revision, each required reader, its reload boundary, and the configuration revision that reader reports using. An unchanged or unobserved reader remains pending or unknown. New values apply at the supported reload boundary; they do not alter authority already pinned to an in-flight attempt.
>
> **Recovery and rollback.** The operation links authorization, candidate, publication run, resulting commit and adoption observations. After an interruption, reconciliation checks those records before repeating a side effect. A lost response does not create a second publication run or duplicate application. Uncertain outcomes remain explicit. A rollback is another authorized reviewed change, preserving unrelated changes made meanwhile.
>
> **Drift and doctor.** The configuration baseline retains the identity and contents of the originally installed bundle. Applying an operational change does not regenerate that baseline from current effective configuration. A missing baseline is recovered only from evidence of the original bundle; otherwise it remains unknown.
>
> Drift retains its existing comparison and separately cites the role’s decision and delivered change. Doctor distinguishes invalid configuration, unsupported values, pending publication, committed but unadopted values, and observed adoption. Neither a role’s authorization nor a successful commit proves that a service uses the value.

Intended and executed coverage remain recorded against the verified revision.

## Context

The fixed-roles ruling held that authority a project could declare is authority a project could widen. It was right, and it also makes every specialist - an observer, an assessor - a harness code change, which does not scale to other people's projects.

**Decision.** Authority semantics stay in trusted Go as capability primitives plus runtime separation policy. Ordinary configuration still cannot touch authority. What becomes configurable — protected, operator-activated, digest-pinned, and only after authorization-by-capability reaches behavioral parity with the five shipped roles — is the composition of known primitives into named bundles.

**Rejected.** Roles fixed as Go constants forever: blocks specialists behind code changes and invites bespoke orchestration per specialist, which is the pattern this whole design retires. Authority in ordinary configuration or personas: rejected before, still rejected, and now enforced by invariant. A plugin API for new primitives: rejected — a primitive's semantics must be implemented and reviewed in-tree, because somebody must be accountable for what a capability means.

**Consequences.** The parity sequence in the configurable-workflows design is binding: the authority inventory and capability registry land before anything is configurable, authorization call sites convert from role names to capability-and-scope checks before operator-defined bundles load, and the closed role-name type is removed last. Durable records created under the original five names keep compatibility decoding. The harness design's fixed-roles statement gains the refinement rather than being erased.

## Owner decisions: subsequent ruling

Owning-role amendment decisions (yoyodyne-ifd.437.14) adds the following ruling. The original decision above remains the record of the capability model's introduction; this addition records the specific authority needed for autonomous document ownership.

**Choice.** The harness exposes a typed amendment-decision capability to the shipped roles that own governed documents, scoped by the canonical ownership table, product, repository, document identity, and current revision. Trusted code derives the actor from the invoking conversation or other authenticated entry point. An agent-supplied role name, persona, configuration setting, or path grant cannot supply this capability or widen its scope.

The architect decides amendments to architect-owned documents within approved goals. The Lead Product Manager decides amendments within the intent already delegated to that role. Fundamental intent changes remain reserved to the operator and are drafted by the Lead Product Manager. The operator retains direct intervention and a separately recorded override on any document. An assistant cannot impersonate that intervention.

**Why this follows.** The standing autonomy goal requires routine decisions to remain with their owning roles. The existing capability principle already says that the harness performs an authorized operation on a role's behalf. Recording that role's document decision is such an operation; it is not configuration granting new authority.

**Rejected alternatives.** Keeping every proposal on the operator's queue makes document ownership advisory and retains routine human work. Having an assistant approve on the operator's behalf falsifies who decided. Treating a role string in an output block as authorization lets untrusted content confer authority. Automatically applying a proposal's prose turns downstream advice into an upstream edit. All four are rejected.

**Enforcement.** Every decision entry point uses the same authorization, serialization, expected-state comparison, durable operation identity, and recovery rules in the [artifact contract](../designs/artifact-contract.md). Record the actual decider separately from the owning authority. Concurrent callers cannot each claim an effective ordinary decision; retries recover the same operation. Operator overrides retain the prior decision and name the expected effective decision explicitly.

The first ordinary decision retains its meaning for legacy records. Unsupported record versions and damaged authoritative history cause a visible refusal rather than silent omission. Historical recommendations require source recovery and present owner reconciliation; they are not backdated decisions.

**Separation.** Amendment approval settles a proposal, not a document. The owner authors the resulting revision. Independent review and revision-bound integration checks govern its publication. Approval does not mint check evidence, a review verdict, integration authority, or permission to overwrite a changed document. Report the decision afterwards and distinguish it from revision and landing.
